headline: High-risk default interaction: transformers can read/write and egress broadly, while the prompt-engineering repo can seed untrusted instructions that may be treated as content or guidance.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing repository with prompt-related materials, and agent B can read files, run browsers, and process stdin/stdout. A plausible bridge exists if A’s content is fed into B as instructions or examples, but no shared channel is documented, so I avoid claiming a stronger pathway.
conditions: IF agent A’s repository content is copied into agent B’s prompt or pipeline input, THEN instruction hijacking becomes plausible.
IF agent B parses file or stdin content as trusted guidance, THEN prompt injection risk materializes.
mitigations: Restrict B to treat A-originated text as data, not instructions.
Add a fixed delimiter and system prompt wrapper for any A→B handoff.
Review one sample A document before feeding it into B.
Disable browser-driven ingestion for untrusted prompt corpora.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between A and B inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B has broad filesystem and network egress, but agent A is only a docs-only content-writing repo with no touched data classes. There is no documented shared workspace or sensitive data flow, so leakage is limited to unusual operator setup rather than default exposure.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local workspace, THEN B can read files produced by A.
IF A is used to curate sensitive text and B is allowed to upload it, THEN exfiltration becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories.
Run B with network egress disabled for shared corpora.
Audit one output file before any upload step.
Use a throwaway workspace for A-generated artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; agent A is a content-writing repo that may generate or curate files. If both are placed on the same writable path, conflicts are plausible. Because A has no explicit write surface, I do not escalate beyond medium.
conditions: IF A and B share a writable directory, THEN concurrent edits can collide.
IF B writes generated artifacts into A’s repo, THEN file clobbering or state drift can occur.
mitigations: Use separate output directories.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Check git status before and after B runs.
Keep generated files out of the source tree.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can supply prompt or content-writing material, and agent B can execute pipelines and browsers. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or generated documents. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF B consumes A’s output without verification, THEN incorrect instructions can propagate.
IF B uses A-generated text in a browser or pipeline step, THEN downstream mistakes can multiply.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B.
Require B to cite source provenance before acting.
Compare A output against a known-good template.
Limit B to read-only processing of A output.
requires-engineering: add automated validation of A→B handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source docs-only artifacts with no explicit PHI, residency, or retention commitments. The main compliance concern is operational: B’s broad egress could move A-derived content outside intended boundaries, but the profiles do not show a concrete regulated-data mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into A’s content and then processed by B, THEN compliance obligations may apply.
IF B uploads A-derived artifacts to external services, THEN retention/residency controls must be checked.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in A’s corpus.
Disable B egress for sensitive runs.
Confirm retention settings before upload.
Keep a local-only workflow for compliance-sensitive material.
requires-engineering: document data-flow and residency controls.
